records.observation: Drawable subclass stores Primitive array. Sized constructors set final index; array-input constructor shares array and explicit bounds but does not set last_prime_idx or child parents. resolveCategory calls every nonnull child before AND accumulation (unlike Shadow short-circuit). getByteSize includes own inherited+2 only when category nonnull, whereas write always writes inherited data/count; caller context needed. write sorts shared array in-place by start order, narrows count to signed short and writes primitives. read allocates signed count, sets each child parent, expands bounds without reset, sets final index. Setters retain references/expand bounds, do not set parents; whole-array setter checks equal size. Line IDs use sorted deduplicated TreeSet and typed array. First/final vertex use first/cached final child. isTimeOrdered checks inherited bounds, child validity and covers, using narrowed short length; no adjacent child ordering check. addPrimitivesToSet uses short length and overlap filter. Rendering/hit methods use endpoint times, row/nesting height or mapped endpoint rows, delegate State/Arrow/Line/Event; search delegates category. toString prints all child primitives; synthetic accessor exposes array. Local unset-index/narrowing/size mismatch observations require caller analysis; archived application not executed.

records.observation: Iterator stores outer composite and timeframe reference, index zero, prefetched next. Null array gives null prefetch; empty array terminates. getNextInQueue tests overlap at current index; false branches directly back to offset0 without increment, so a non-overlapping current primitive causes a non-progressing loop while inputs remain unchanged. Index increments only on successful overlap. Constructor prefetch and next prefetch can enter this loop; next may fail to return previously saved item. hasNext checks cached nonnull; exhausted nonnull array next returns null; null-array next dereferences array. remove no-op. No skip/snapshot/concurrent modification handling. This is direct bytecode control-flow evidence, not an executed application or proven normal-call failure.
